text: Suppose we have a function $T:\real^3\to\real^2$ that has the form $$ T\left(\threevec{x_1}{x_2}{x_3}\right) = \begin{bmatrix} -4x_1 -x_2 + 2x_3 \\ x_1 + 2x_2 - x_3 \\ \end{bmatrix}. $$ We may write $$ \begin{aligned} T\left(\threevec{x_1}{x_2}{x_3}\right) \amp {}={} \begin{bmatrix} -4x_1 -x_2 + 2x_3 \\ x_1 + 2x_2 - x_3 \\ \end{bmatrix} \\ \amp {}={} \twovec{-4x_1}{x_1} + \twovec{-x_2}{2x_2} + \twovec{2x_3}{-x_3} \\ \amp {}={} x_1\twovec{-4}1 + x_2\twovec{-1}2 + x_3\twovec2{-1} \\ \amp{}={} \begin{bmatrix} -4 \amp -1 \amp 2 \\ 1 \amp 2 \amp -1 \\ \end{bmatrix} \threevec{x_1}{x_2}{x_3}. \end{aligned} $$ This shows that $T$ is a matrix transformation $T(\xvec) = A\xvec$ associated to the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} -4 \amp -1 \amp 2 \\ 1 \amp 2 \amp -1 \\ \end{bmatrix}. $
